speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation, could you please describe the specific skin lesions you are concerned about, including their location, appearance, and how long they have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. I would like to examine the lesions closely now; may I look at both the penile lesion and the one on your finger to assess their borders and texture?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless nature of the lesions, combined with their location on the genitals and fingers, raises suspicion for a viral etiology. Do you recall having any contact with animal hides, meat, or hunting activities, and have you noticed any similar lesions on your palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant smoking history and the chronic, non-healing nature of these painless lesions, I am concerned about squamous cell carcinoma. Has the lesion on your penis been present for more than six months, and have you noticed any bleeding or ulceration?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the location of the lesions and your origin, I need to ask if you have ever practiced female genital mutilation or were circumcised, as this is a significant risk factor for penile cancer. Also, have you noticed any enlarged lymph nodes in your groin area?
